The hourglass drum is a class of membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 211.24, also called a waisted drum. It has an hourglass shape, the head is fastened with cords, and during playing the cords can be squeezed to change pitch. The category covers different drums in most parts of the world, including some pellet drums such as the damaru; but not every pellet drum is hourglass-shaped — the Korean do, nodo, noedo and yeongdo, for example, are barrel-shaped. The hourglass drum is a generic term and does not denote one particular instrument; construction, size, use and playing method differ from place to place.
沙漏鼓是膜鳴樂器中的泛稱類別，並非源自單一地區或特定統一樂器。其存在於世界多數地: The hourglass drum is a generic class among membranophones; it does not come from one region and is not one uniform instrument. It exists in most parts of the world, and construction, size, use and playing method vary widely. Drums of this class are marked by an hourglass or waisted shape, a head fastened with cords, and a pitch the player changes by squeezing those cords. It also includes bead drums such as the damaru, but not every bead drum is hourglass-shaped — some Korean drums, for example, are barrel-shaped. The hourglass drum therefore serves mainly to classify instruments rather than to refer to one historical tradition.
